title: Module builder: author a form with sample pre-fill + Health Canada review
walkthrough:
You land on a dossier list page under a top bar reading "ANDS Studio" with chips for "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence" and "Guided journey →". The heading is "Your product dossiers"; you click "New dossier +". A card asks for "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456") and "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"). Fine print explains Health Canada issues the ID via REP/CESG; if you type a wrong format you get "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)". A small link, "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →", generates a draft ID you can rename later. You press "Create & open →".

You arrive in a three-pane module workspace: a left rail listing every eCTD section with status glyphs and "req"/"opt" badges plus a collapsed "Not required for this generic" group; a centre panel; a right rail showing module progress ("required sections complete"), a filing gate with "Documents", "Fee" and "Valid eCTD" check flags, and sequence/validation cards.

Clicking a section shows its title, purpose, and a guidance box headed "What Health Canada needs here" with a link "Health Canada guidance ↗", expected formats and a bilingual flag where applicable. An action bar offers "⬆ Upload", "✦ Author in-app" and "⊘ Mark N/A".

You choose "✦ Author in-app". For AI-draftable prose sections a second toggle appears — "💬 Draft with AI" versus "✦ Sample & edit". In the form mode, a note reads "Pre-filled with a realistic sample from your dossier — edit every field to your product, then author." Fields (e.g. "Drug product", "Sponsor company", "Canadian Reference Product (brand)", "AUC 90% CI") arrive pre-populated; worked-example values carry a small "sample" tag you're expected to replace. Two buttons follow: "Author [section title] →" (showing "Authoring…" while busy) and "Review vs Health Canada".

Authoring generates the document and immediately runs the review. A result banner reads "Health Canada review:" then either "no blocking content gaps." or a count of items "to fix" and "to check", with each finding listed (✗ or ⚠), a suggested edit, and an "HC guidance ↗" link. You can also run "Review vs Health Canada" on demand before authoring.

The finished document appears as a row with filename, size, an md5 checksum prefix, a provenance chip — "authored in-app", "uploaded", or "AI-assisted — review before filing" — and a "Download" link. Knowing the real Health Canada Dossier ID format (one letter plus 6–7 digits) is required to move off the placeholder.
